places.name: Eiffel Tower
places.description: An iconic lattice tower, an architectural landmark and observation tower with views of the city.
places.evidence: The Eiffel Tower is a lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France.

places.name: Louvre Museum
places.description: An art museum featuring archaeological collections and works spanning ancient art to paintings.
places.evidence: The Louvre is a national art museum in Paris, France.

places.name: Notre-Dame de Paris
places.description: A Gothic cathedral located on the Île de la Cité, representing medieval French architecture.
places.evidence: Notre-Dame de Paris, often referred to simply as Notre-Dame, is a medieval Catholic cathedral and basilica on the Île de la Cité, in the 4th arrondissement of Paris, France.

places.name: Musée d'Orsay
places.description: A former railway station converted into an art museum specializing in works from the Impressionist period.
places.evidence: The Musée d'Orsay is a museum in Paris, France, on the Left Bank of the Seine.

places.name: Arc de Triomphe
places.description: A triumphal arch in neoclassical style, a symbol of French cultural identity.
places.evidence: The Arc de Triomphe de l'Étoile, often simply called the Arc de Triomphe, is one of the most famous monuments in Paris, France.

places.name: Café de Flore
places.description: One of the oldest and most celebrated coffeehouses, known for its emblematic shopfront and famous clientele.
places.evidence: Thé Café de Flore is one of the oldest coffeehouses in Paris, known for its emblematic shopfront and celebrated for its famous clientele, which in the past included influential writers, philosophers, and members of Parisian high society (tout-Paris).

places.name: Angelina
places.description: A popular tea house and café known for its almost pudding-like hot chocolate and its Mont Blanc dessert.
places.evidence: Angelina is a popular tea house and café with several locations in Paris and one location in NYC.

places.name: Bibliothèque nationale de France
places.description: The national library of France, one of the oldest libraries in the world.
places.evidence: The Bibliothèque nationale de France is the national library of France, located in Paris on two main sites, Richelieu and François-Mitterrand.

places.name: French Open
places.description: An annual grand slam tennis tournament held in spring at Roland Garros.
places.evidence: The French Open, also known as Roland-Garros, is a tennis tournament organized by the French Tennis Federation annually at Stade Roland Garros in Paris, France.

city_tips.title: Paris has an excellent metro
city_tips.content: The Métro and RER move millions of people daily at affordable rates with frequent service.
city_tips.evidence: The Métro and RER move staggering numbers of people into, out of, and around Paris (6.75 million people per day on average), and most of the time in reasonable comfort.

city_tips.title: Book Restaurants Well Ahead
city_tips.content: Trendy Paris restaurants often need reservations weeks or months ahead; a lunch reservation is usually easier and cheaper to get.
city_tips.evidence: Trendy restaurants often require reservations weeks, if not months in advance. If you haven't planned far enough ahead, try to get a reservation for lunch which is generally easier and less expensive.

city_tips.title: Avoid crowded transit areas
city_tips.content: The metro and RER are popular targets for pickpockets, so stay alert on crowded trains and platforms.
city_tips.evidence: The métro and RER are also a popular place for pickpockets.

city_tips.title: Enjoy local cafes
city_tips.content: Traditional bistros with sidewalk terraces offer simple, reasonably priced meat-centred meals across the city.
city_tips.evidence: there are hundreds of traditional bistros, with their sidewalk terraces offering a choice of fairly simple (usually meat centred) meals for reasonable prices

places.name: British Museum
places.description: The world-renowned national museum housing treasures from ancient civilizations in a neoclassical building.
places.evidence: The British Museum is a public museum dedicated to human history, art and culture located in the Bloomsbury area of London.

places.name: Buckingham Palace
places.description: The official London residence of the British monarch, the principal working palace of the reigning sovereign.
places.evidence: Buckingham Palace is the official residence and administrative headquarters of the monarch of the United Kingdom in London, England.

places.name: Tower of London
places.description: An historic fortress housing the Crown Jewels and royal armory, a museum and castle.
places.evidence: The Tower of London, officially His Majesty's Royal Palace and Fortress of the Tower of London, is a historic citadel and castle on the north bank of the River Thames in London, England.

places.name: Westminster Abbey
places.description: A spectacular Gothic church serving as a burial site of monarchs, an abbey church.
places.evidence: Westminster Abbey, formally titled the Collegiate Church of Saint Peter at Westminster, is an Anglican church in the City of Westminster, London, England.

places.name: Tower Bridge
places.description: A bascule and suspension bridge spanning the River Thames in gothic revival style.
places.evidence: Tower Bridge is a Grade I listed combined bascule, suspension, and, until 1960, cantilever bridge in London, built between 1886 and 1894, designed by Horace Jones and engineered by John Wolfe Barry with the help of Henry Marc Brunel.

places.name: Restaurant Gordon Ramsay
places.description: A restaurant serving refined cuisine in an intimate setting.
places.evidence: Restaurant Gordon Ramsay, also known as Gordon Ramsay at Royal Hospital Road, is the signature restaurant of the British celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay at Royal Hospital Road, in Chelsea, London.

places.name: Bar Italia
places.description: A historic Italian cafe in Soho, famous for traditional Italian coffee and pastries.
places.evidence: Bar Italia is an Italian café located on Frith Street in the Soho district of London, United Kingdom.

places.name: Wong Kei
places.description: A legendary Cantonese restaurant in Soho, known for authentic Chinese cuisine.
places.evidence: Wong Kei is a Chinese restaurant in London's Chinatown, once described as "the rudest restaurant in London".

places.name: Wimbledon Championships
places.description: The world's oldest tennis tournament held annually featuring grass courts.
places.evidence: The Wimbledon Championships, commonly called Wimbledon, is a tennis tournament organised annually in Wimbledon, London, by the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club in collaboration with the Lawn Tennis Association.

city_tips.title: Use public transport effectively
city_tips.content: A contactless bank card is often the most convenient way to pay for buses, the Tube and trains, priced the same as an Oyster card.
city_tips.evidence: Contactless debit/credit card (your normal bank card) is often the most convenient approach, and priced the same as Oyster card.

city_tips.title: Book Around Major Events
city_tips.content: Hotel prices spike close to major sporting tournaments like Wimbledon or big football fixtures, so plan or book well ahead around such events.
city_tips.evidence: Prices invariably become inflated close to major sporting tournaments (such as the London Marathon, Wimbledon or major England football/rugby fixtures), or other important events taking place in the city

city_tips.title: Watch Your Belongings
city_tips.content: Keep normal precautions for your belongings: begging, drug abuse and phone-snatching theft occur in London like in any big city.
city_tips.evidence: Like many big cities, London has a variety of social problems, especially begging, drug abuse and theft; mobile phones are a favourite target, often snatched by fast-moving moped riders

city_tips.title: Diverse food options
city_tips.content: The city offers a rich multicultural dining scene with cuisines from around the world.
city_tips.evidence: As London is one of the world's most multicultural cities, it is possible to find virtually every cuisine from around the world here if you look hard enough.

places.name: Belém Tower
places.description: A fortified tower on the Tagus River serving as a defensive fortress and architectural heritage monument.
places.evidence: Belém Tower, officially the Tower of Saint Vincent, is a 16th-century fortification located in Lisbon, Portugal, which served as a point of embarkation and disembarkation for Portuguese explorers and as a ceremonial gateway to Lisbon.

places.description: A Portuguese monastery representing cultural heritage and monastic architecture.

places.name: Vasco da Gama Bridge

places.evidence: The Vasco da Gama Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge flanked by viaducts that spans the Tagus River in Parque das Nações in Lisbon, the capital of Portugal.

places.name: Alfama

places.evidence: The Alfama is the oldest neighborhood of Lisbon, spreading on the slope between the São Jorge Castle and the Tagus river.

places.name: 25 de Abril Bridge

places.evidence: The 25 de Abril Bridge is a suspension bridge connecting the city of Lisbon, capital of Portugal, with the municipality of Almada on the left (south) bank of the Tagus River.

city_tips.title: Use public transport
city_tips.content: The integrated Navegante card provides seamless access across metro, buses, and trams throughout the city.
city_tips.evidence: Most public transport in Lisbon uses an integrated ticketing system, allowing the same smartcard to be used across metro, buses, trams, suburban trains and many ferries.

city_tips.title: Try fresh seafood
city_tips.content: Head to the 'seafood strip' on Rua das Portas de Santo Antão, near Praça dos Restauradores, for fresh seafood restaurants.
city_tips.evidence: the Rua das Portas de Santo Antão, a 'seafood strip' northeast from and parallel to Praça dos Restauradores

city_tips.title: Lisbon Has Good Budget Hostels
city_tips.content: Lisbon has clean, active hostels citywide, with prices in the historic center starting around 30 euros and cheaper further out.
city_tips.evidence: Lisbon sets high standards for budget accommodation, with numerous clean and active hostels around the city. Prices in the historical center start around €30

city_tips.title: Skip Costly Tourist Buses
city_tips.content: Instead of a costly tourist bus, ride tram line 28 through the Old Town from Graca down to Alfama and Baixa.
city_tips.evidence: Instead of paying for a ride on one of the costly tourist buses, try line 28, which winds its way through the "Old Town" of Lisbon beginning in Graça then down to the Alfama and to the Baixa

city_tips.title: Walk in historic center
city_tips.content: Medieval streets have uneven surfaces, so wear supportive shoes for comfortable exploration.

city_tips.title: Protect valuables on transit
city_tips.content: Exercise caution on crowded metro trains where thieves operate in organized groups.
city_tips.evidence: Pickpocketing on the Metro is rife in the form of gangs of young girls (8 to 15 years old), often pregnant, who jump on the trains just as they are about to leave.

city_tips.title: Plan travel wisely
city_tips.content: Check accommodation pricing for your specific dates to find the best rates.
city_tips.evidence: Always check prices at your accommodation for your specific dates.

city_tips.title: Avoid Restaurant Tourist Traps
city_tips.content: Guidebook-recommended restaurants can be inflated 'tourist traps'; look for places in residential areas away from major sights instead.
city_tips.evidence: Restaurants in guidebooks can be good but prices can be inflated because it is more than likely a "tourist trap".
